docs.text: I feel like I'm stretching the scope of your question but I'd love to see a timeline exploring the consequences of more successful Native resistance to encroaching settlement in the great lakes region, e.g. the Haudenosaunee do better during/after the AmRev or maybe Tecumseh is more successful?

And the romanticization of the American frontier casually elides over the fact that the incredibly welcoming forest around the Great Lakes down through Appalachia was the abandoned silviculture/agriculture of the Great Dying of First Nations people. Virgin field infection is brutal.

Before the European invasion, much of North America, from the Gulf of Mexico to the Great Lakes, was a cultivated and carefully managed agroforest, teeming with abundant flora and fauna to gather and hunt; it was not a pristine wilderness untouched by the hands of humans
